expl1: DNS is described as the internet's address book that maps web addresses to site addresses
Browser cache stores recently visited sites for instant access
If the cache misses, the request goes to a recursive resolver
The root server points the resolver to the top-level domain server (e.g., .com or .org)
The authoritative server holds the exact address for the site
The resolver returns the answer to the device and caches it
TTL stands for time to live and controls how long the answer is stored
Cached answers make the next visit faster
The whole process happens in a fraction of a second

these features stretch the 3,000 cycles across years of everyday use
